# U.S. English editorial standard

Use **U.S. English (en-US)** for all original repository prose, documentation, UI strings, customer-facing descriptions, release notes, comments, tests, and AI-generated copy. Consistently write color, behavior, optimize, analyze, organization, authorization, license, center, gray, canceled, and modeled. In Formula 1 material, use tire and tires.

Keep writing clear and natural; review assistant-generated copy before committing it. This applies to changes in code comments, Markdown, HTML, product messaging, emails, README files, and issue/PR descriptions.

**Safety and compatibility:** Preserve exact external API names, published schema fields, data identifiers, third-party package names, quotations, filenames, legal notices, trademarks, licensed material, and proper names when spelling changes would break behavior or distort a source. Change a public identifier only with an explicit compatibility migration and tests. Do not blindly rewrite entire codebases.
